blocks.content: The velocity of seismic waves changes as they travel through materials with different densities.

items: S-waves cannot pass through liquids, providing direct proof that the Earth's outer core is in a molten state.
Memorize the order of discontinuities from surface to core: Conrad (Crust), Mohorovičić (Crust-Mantle), Repetti (Upper-Lower Mantle), Gutenberg (Mantle-Core), and Lehmann (Outer-Inner Core).
The P-wave shadow zone forms a distinct band between 105° and 145° from the earthquake epicenter.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Direct sources of information about the interior include surface rocks, deep mining, ocean drilling projects, and volcanic eruptions.
Indirect sources include meteoric evidence, gravitational anomalies, magnetic field surveys, and seismic wave behavior.
Primary (P) waves are longitudinal and travel through solids, liquids, and gases, whereas Secondary (S) waves are transverse and travel only through solids.
The Earth's structure is divided into three main layers: the Crust (Sial/Sima), the Mantle (Asthenosphere and Mesosphere), and the Core (Outer liquid and Inner solid NIFE).
Seismic wave shadow zones reveal the internal structure, with the S-wave shadow zone extending beyond 105° from the epicenter.
